headline: Edge appliances carry the day as exploited flaws stack up across firewalls, VPNs and mail gateways
standfirst: Every CVE in this selection — five distinct identifiers — is CISA KEV-listed and marked as known-exploited, and three of the affected products sit on the network edge. Two further stories involve real exploitation but arrived without CVE identifiers in the material supplied. The through-line is not novelty but incompleteness: partial fixes, layered chains, and implants that outlive the patch.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

Lead with PAN-OS [[s30]]. CVE-2026-0322 is a code-injection flaw (CWE-94) rated 8.6 High under CVSS 4.0, and it has been exploited against firewalls. NVD places it in the management interface and says it lets an authenticated attacker with network access execute arbitrary code as root — so this is not an anonymous internet-wide hit: exploitation depends on both credentials and reachability of the management plane. Affected configurations include PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and Panorama; Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are listed as not impacted. CISA added it to KEV with a required action built around vendor mitigations and per-asset exposure evaluation, and a federal remediation deadline only days later. Analysis: the operative question is whether a management interface is reachable beyond trusted internal addresses — the same exposure the vendor's own guidance tells operators to close. That deadline binds federal agencies under the cited directive, not everyone.

Cisco patched a Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in attacks [[s41]], where a crafted email attachment lets remote unauthenticated attackers run commands with root privileges. No CVE identifier, affected versions or remediation detail was supplied here, so verify against the vendor advisory; what's clear is the appliance's position in the path of untrusted mail.

Ivanti Connect Secure carries CVE-2026-104935 [[s32]]: an authentication bypass by spoofing (CWE-290), 8.6 High under CVSS 3.1, remotely exploitable with no privileges and no user interaction, leading to arbitrary command execution. NVD lists ICS before 25.1.3.0 as affected, and 22.7R2.14 and earlier as not impacted. The excerpt says the issue was only partially identified and patched earlier, leaving a window attackers used. Analysis: an incomplete fix on an edge device is close to no fix at all. KEV-listed, with a federal remediation deadline shortly after addition.

AhsayCBS has new fixes after earlier patches proved incomplete [[s27]], with two KEV-listed flaws reported as exploited to drop web shells and XMRig miners. CVE-2026-105133 is improper authentication at 5.5 Medium; CVE-2026-105134 is OS command injection at 9.3 Critical. The excerpt says they can be chained to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary commands. NVD points to upgrading to 10.3.4. Note the severity split is real: the Medium is the way in, the Critical is what happens next.

## Breaches

The UK Legal Aid Agency breach now reaches records going back to 1978 [[s23]]. The agency is an executive agency of the Ministry of Justice that manages the Public Defender Service, and the excerpt attributes the intrusion to attackers who breached its IT systems during a 2025 incident. Analysis: depth of history is the story — decades-old records widen identity-fraud exposure and the accountability question, since material that old was almost certainly never designed to be defended by current controls. No record count, data categories or affected-population figures were supplied.

## Vulnerabilities

Next.js shipped an out-of-band update fixing two critical flaws that allow unauthenticated remote code execution, plus a high-severity denial-of-service issue [[s10]]. One RCE is in React Server Components; the other is in librsvg, the library Next.js uses through the sharp package to handle SVG images. No CVE identifiers or version ranges appear in the supplied material. For web teams, the useful triage signal is the delivery model: an out-of-band release means the vendor judged normal cycle timing unacceptable.

## Industry

The US Department of Justice disrupted the Famous Chollima group's operations, arresting two suspects, charging 14 individuals and seizing nearly 187 laptops used in North Korean remote IT worker schemes, with the action tied to Texas [[s37]]. Analysis: the significance is enforcement pressure on the logistics layer — the laptops and intermediaries — rather than on the intrusion tradecraft itself. The material does not detail charges, dispositions or which employers were affected.

## Research

A new research report documents PEERSTITCH, a memory-resident ARM64 implant deployed to more than 500 FortiGate firewalls via CVE-2024-47575 [[s31]]. That CVE is a missing-authentication flaw in FortiManager rated 9.8 Critical and KEV-listed since 2024. One discrepancy in the supplied material is worth flagging: the vulnerability is described as a FortiManager issue while the reported targets are FortiGate firewalls, and nothing supplied reconciles the two. Analysis: with no new CVE at the centre of this story, its value is tradecraft — memory residency and long dwell on edge hardware — and the reminder that older KEV entries remain live intrusion paths long after the patch window closes.

kev.vulnerabilityName: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS Code Injection Vulnerability
kev.shortDescription: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS contains a code injection vulnerability that could allow an authenticated attacker with network access to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the firewall.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. nvd.description:
A remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in the management interface of Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS® software enables an authenticated attacker with network access to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the firewall.



The security risk posed by this issue is minimized by restricting access to the management interface to only trusted internal IP addresses according to our recommended  best practice deployment guidelines https://live.paloaltonetworks.com/t5/community-blogs/tips-amp-tricks-how-to-secure-the-management-access-of-your-palo/ba-p/464431 .



This issue is applicable to PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama (virtual and M-Series).



Cloud NGFW and Prisma® Access are not impacted by this vulnerability.

nvd.description: Langflow is a tool for building and deploying AI-powered agents and workflows. Prior to 1.9.0, any authenticated Langflow user can achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the server by adding an MCP server with the "Stdio" transport. The user-supplied command field is passed directly to bash -c "exec {command}" with zero validation, no allowlisting, and no sandboxing. The command executes immediately when the server list is fetched. Additionally, the env field allows arbitrary environment variable injection (e.g., LD_PRELOAD, PATH override). This vulnerability is fixed in 1.9.0.
